subject: WLSMV versus MLR - Intercepts of manifested items fixed to 0

messages.author: 8c33b73eab5b37ef
messages.subject: WLSMV versus MLR - Intercepts of manifested items fixed to 0
parts:
Hi,
What is the theoretical explanation for the fact that when running a CFA with ordered categorical measures (estimator = WLSMV), we get the item intercepts fixed to 0, but not with MLR?
In both cases, the latent means are naturally constrained to 0, but the items differ.
Why is that?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: WLSMV versus MLR - Intercepts of manifested items fixed to 0
parts:
It is an identification constraint for the latent response.  There is no latent response when using MLR (i.e., when treating the observations as numeric).

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/CatMGLong.pdf

https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3162326/
